items.note: Uses D-MIGHT, D-THINK-THAT, G-INSOFAR. lehse and kat ba nga tip are the hedges; ngam tip shisha (I don't know for sure) closes the hedge.

items.target: Shisha hi ba ___, hynrei ___ / Nga mynjur ïa kata, hynrei ___
items.gloss: It is true that ___, but ___ / I grant that, but ___

example.target: Shisha hi ba ka dor ka jrong, hynrei ka kali ka sah bun snem.
example.gloss: It's true the price is high, but the car lasts many years.

items.note: Uses C-ADMITTEDLY, G-HOWEVER, C-TAKE-YOUR-POINT. Khasi concedes with shisha hi (truly indeed) and always counters with hynrei in the same breath.

items.target: Wat sheptieng, ___ / Nga kular ba ___ / Kan long bha, ngeit ïa nga
items.gloss: Don't be afraid, ___ / I promise that ___ / It'll be fine, trust me

example.target: Wat sheptieng, kan long bha. Nga kular ba ngan sah bad phi.
example.gloss: Don't worry, it'll be fine. I promise I'll stay with you.

items.note: Uses T-IMPERATIVE, D-WILL, D-VERB-TO. Reassurance is a wat imperative plus a future promise; ngeit ïa nga (trust me) seals it.

items.target: Ha kawei ka liang ___, ha kawei pat ka liang ___ / Haba peit ïa baroh ar liang, ___
items.gloss: On one side ___, on the other side ___ / Looking at both sides, ___

example.target: Ha kawei ka liang ka nongbah ka suk, ha kawei pat ka liang ki dukan ki duh.
example.gloss: On one side the city is quiet, on the other side the shops lose.

items.note: Uses G-OTHER-HAND, G-WHEREAS, C-ON-BALANCE. liang is side; pat (again, in turn) marks the second side. The verdict follows haba peit ïa baroh.

items.target: Lehse u la ___ / U dei ban la ___ / Um lah ban la ___
items.gloss: Maybe he has ___ / He must have ___ / He can't have ___

example.target: Lehse u la klet; u dei ban la sah ha ïing, namar ba ka phone jong u kam trei.
example.gloss: Maybe he forgot; he must have stayed at home, because his phone isn't working.

items.note: Uses D-MUST-HAVE, D-COULD-HAVE, G-OR. Speculation is an adverb (lehse) or dei ban / lah ban with la; the verb itself never changes.

items.target: Lada tang nga la ___ / Lada nga la tip, ngan la ___
items.gloss: If only I had ___ / If I had known, I would have ___

example.target: Lada tang nga la shim kata ka kam! Lada nga la tip, ngan la ong hooid.
example.gloss: If only I had taken that job! If I had known, I would have said yes.

items.note: Uses D-WISH-HAD, D-IF-HAD-KNOWN, T-COND3. Regret is lada tang plus la; the counterfactual result is yn la (ngan la ong, I would have said).

items.target: Nga pan ïa phi ban ___ / Nga kyrpad ba phi ___ / haduh ka sngi ___
items.gloss: I request you to ___ / I plead that you ___ / by the ___ (date)

example.target: Nga pan ïa phi ban pynkhreh ïa ka heater haduh Friday; lada em, ngan ïathuh ïa ka ophis.
example.gloss: I request you to repair the heater by Friday; if not, I'll inform the office.

items.note: Uses C-I-WONDER-IF, D-HAVE-IT-DONE, G-AS-LONG-AS. Written requests use pan (request) and kyrpad (plead) with phi; the consequence clause opens with lada em (if not).

items.target: lada nga la tip, ngan la ___
items.gloss: if I had known, I would have ___

example.target: Lada nga la tip ba phi don hangne, ngan la wan kham shwa.
example.gloss: If I had known you were here, I would have come earlier.

items.note: The third conditional is lada plus la in the if-clause and yn la (future plus past) in the result: ngan la wan. This yn la is the only 'would have' Khasi has.

items.target: ka dei ban la ___ / kam lah ban la ___
items.gloss: she must have ___ / she can't have ___

example.target: Ka dei ban la klet ïa ka meeting; kam lah ban la leit noh khlem ong.
example.gloss: She must have forgotten the meeting; she can't have left without saying.

items.note: Same shape as D-MUST-BE with la after ban. Everyday speech prefers lehse ka la klet (maybe she forgot) or shisha ka la klet (surely she forgot).

items.target: ngan lah ___ dep haduh ___
items.gloss: I will have finished ___ by ___

example.target: Ngan lah thoh dep ïa ka kot haduh u bnai December.
example.gloss: I will have finished writing the book by December.

items.note: yn plus lah plus verb plus dep (finished) is the future perfect; haduh gives the deadline. Without dep, ngan lah thoh just means 'I'll be done writing'.

items.target: ngan dang ___ ha ___
items.gloss: I will be ___-ing at ___

example.target: U snem ba wan ha kane ka por, ngan dang trei ha Sohra.
example.gloss: This time next year, I'll be working in Sohra.

items.note: yn plus dang. It sounds heavy; most speakers simply say ngan trei ha Sohra with the time phrase carrying the meaning.

items.target: nga la dang ___ naduh ___ / nga la dang ___ kat ___
items.gloss: I had been ___-ing since ___ / for ___

example.target: Nga la dang ap kat shi kynta shwa ba ka bas ka poi.
example.gloss: I had been waiting for an hour before the bus arrived.

items.note: la dang plus a duration (kat shi kynta, a full hour) or naduh (since) gives the past perfect progressive. shwa ba supplies the later event.

items.target: nga la ai ban ___ ïa ___ / nga la pynkhreh ïa ___
items.gloss: I had ___ done to ___ / I got ___ repaired

example.target: Nga la ai ban pynkhreh ïa ka kali ha ka dukan.
example.gloss: I had the car repaired at the garage.

items.note: ai ban (give to be done) is the causative frame; the object takes ïa. Many verbs take pyn- instead: pynkhreh (get repaired), pynkhih (get moved).

items.target: lada tang nga la ___ / nga kwah ba nga la ___
items.gloss: if only I had ___ / I wish I had ___

example.target: Lada tang nga la shim kata ka kam u snem ba la leit!
example.gloss: If only I had taken that job last year!

items.note: lada tang (if only) plus la, said as a hanging clause with falling tone. kwah ba nga la is the full-sentence version; there is no separate wish form.

items.target: mynba nga dang khynnah, ngi ju ___ / ngi la ju ___
items.gloss: when I was young, we would ___ / we used to ___

example.target: Mynba nga dang khynnah, ngi ju leit sha wah man ka sngi Saturday.
example.gloss: When I was young, we would go to the river every Saturday.

items.note: ju (habitually) with a mynba clause covers both 'would' and 'used to'. la is optional because mynba already fixes the past.

items.target: u la ong ba um shym la ___ (denied) / u la mynjur ba u la ___
items.gloss: he denied ___-ing / he admitted ___-ing / he suggested ___-ing

example.target: U la ong ba um shym la shim ka pisa, hynrei hadien u la mynjur ba u la shim.
example.gloss: He denied taking the money, but later he admitted he had taken it.

items.note: Reporting verbs take a full ba clause, never an -ing form: deny is 'say that not', admit is mynjur ba (agree that), suggest is ai jingmut ban.

items.target: ka la ai jingmut ïa nga ban ___ / ka la ïathuh ïa nga ban wat ___
items.gloss: she advised me to ___ / she told me not to ___

example.target: U doktor u la ai jingmut ïa nga ban shongthiah bad ban wat trei shi taiew.
example.gloss: The doctor advised me to rest and not to work for a week.

items.note: Advice reports use ai jingmut (give opinion) plus ïa plus ban; the negative keeps the imperative wat inside the clause: ban wat trei.

items.target: ki ong ba ___ / la ong ba ___
items.gloss: they say that ___ / it is said that ___

example.target: Ki ong ba u syiem u la wan na kane ka shnong.
example.gloss: It is said that the king came from this village.

items.note: Impersonal ki (they) replaces the English passive; la ong ba is the written variant. 'He is thought to' is simply ki pyrkhat ba u.

items.target: kaba nga kwah ka long ___ / ka long u ___ uba la ___
items.gloss: what I want is ___ / it was ___ who ___

example.target: Kaba nga kwah ka long tang ka jingsuk. Ka long u Bah uba la ïathuh ïa nga.
example.gloss: What I want is only peace. It was Bah who told me.

items.note: kaba (the thing which) heads the free relative and is echoed by ka long. The it-cleft is ka long plus the noun plus its relative uba/kaba.

items.target: no inversion: ym tang ba nga la ___, hynrei nga la ___ ruh
items.gloss: not only did I ___, but I also ___ (no word-order change)

example.target: Ym tang ba nga la pule, hynrei nga la hikai ruh.
example.gloss: Not only did I study, but I also taught.

items.note: Khasi never inverts subject and verb. Emphasis comes from ym tang ba (not only that) plus hynrei ... ruh, and from stressing the fronted phrase.

items.target: phim la donkam ban ___ / phim la hap ban ___
items.gloss: you needn't have ___ / you didn't have to ___

example.target: Phim la donkam ban thied ka jingbam, nga la shet lah.
example.gloss: You needn't have bought food, I had already cooked.

items.note: ym plus la plus donkam ban is 'didn't need to'; Khasi does not distinguish 'needn't have (but did)' from 'didn't need to', so add a clause if it matters.

items.target: pronoun + yn + lah + verb + dep, haduh ___
items.gloss: future perfect: yn lah plus dep

example.target: Haduh lashai, kin lah pynkhreh dep ïa ka lynti.
example.gloss: By tomorrow, they will have finished repairing the road.

items.note: Three particles line up: yn (future) fused to the pronoun, lah (completed), then the verb and dep. Speech often keeps only kin pynkhreh dep haduh lashai.

items.target: pronoun + yn + dang + verb
items.gloss: future continuous: yn dang

example.target: Ha khyndai baje, ngin dang bam ja.
example.gloss: At nine, we'll be eating.

items.note: yn dang is grammatical but rare. It is used when the ongoing state matters (we'll still be eating); otherwise the plain future is preferred.

items.target: pronoun + la dang + verb + duration or naduh
items.gloss: past perfect continuous: la dang plus a time span

example.target: Ki la dang trei kat lai snem shwa ba ka kompani ka la khang.
example.gloss: They had been working for three years before the company closed.

items.note: The same la dang as the past progressive; the duration (kat lai snem) or naduh turns it into 'had been doing for'. No new form is needed.

items.target: Lada ___ la ___, ___ yn la ___
items.gloss: third conditional: la in the if-clause, yn la in the main clause

example.target: Lada ka bas ka la poi ha por, ngan la poi shwa ka meeting.
example.gloss: If the bus had arrived on time, I would have arrived before the meeting.

items.note: yn la (future plus past, written ngan la, un la, kan la) is the counterfactual result. It is the one place Khasi stacks yn and la on the same verb.

items.target: Lada ___ la ___, ___ yn ___ mynta / Lada ___ (present), ___ yn la ___
items.gloss: mixed conditionals: choose la or bare verb per clause

example.target: Lada nga la pule ka Khasi mynba nga dang khynnah, ngan kren bha mynta.
example.gloss: If I had studied Khasi as a child, I would speak well now.

items.note: Each clause carries its own time: la for a past condition, bare verb plus mynta for a present result. Khasi mixes freely because nothing agrees.

items.target: subject switch + la/yn/dang + verb (+ da agent) / ïoh + verb (get-passive)
items.gloss: passive in all tenses; ïoh (get) for the get-passive

example.target: Ka ïing ka dang shna; kan shna dep haduh u snem ba wan; u la ïoh pynïap.
example.gloss: The house is being built; it'll be finished by next year; he got killed.

items.note: Tense particles go on the passive-like verb as usual: dang shna (is being built), yn shna dep (will be built). ïoh plus verb is the get-passive for things suffered.

items.target: Hynrei, ___ / Wat la kumta, ___
items.gloss: However, ___ / Even so, ___

example.target: Ka dor ka jrong. Hynrei, ka jingbam ka bha shibun.
example.gloss: The price is high. However, the food is very good.

items.note: hynrei at the start of a new sentence is 'however'; wat la kumta (even so) is 'nevertheless'. No comma intonation change follows either.

items.target: wat la don ___, ___ / wat la ___ ruh, ___
items.gloss: despite ___ / in spite of ___

example.target: Wat la don ka slap, ki la leit sha ïew.
example.gloss: Despite the rain, they went to the market.

items.note: Khasi has no noun preposition 'despite'; use wat la plus don (there is) plus the noun, or a full wat la clause. ruh strengthens it.

items.target: ___, hynrei ___ / katba ___, ___
items.gloss: ___, whereas ___ / while ___, ___ (formal)

example.target: Ki riewspah ki ïaid da ka kali, hynrei ki riewduk ki ïaid da ka kjat.
example.gloss: The rich travel by car, whereas the poor go on foot.

items.note: Formal contrast is still hynrei; katba (while) works only when the two facts are also simultaneous. Written Khasi sometimes uses hynrei pat.

items.target: ha kawei ka liang ___, ha kawei pat ka liang ___
items.gloss: on the one side ___, on the other side ___

example.target: Ha kawei ka liang ka nongbah ka suk, ha kawei pat ka liang ki nongdie ki duh.
example.gloss: On the one hand the city is quiet, on the other the traders lose.

items.note: liang is side; kawei ... kawei pat is 'one ... the other again'. Use it once, at the start of each half, not repeatedly.

items.target: lada ym ___ / tang lada ___
items.gloss: unless ___ (if not) / only if ___

example.target: Lada phim leit mynta, phin lait ïa ka bas.
example.gloss: Unless you leave now, you'll miss the bus.

items.note: unless is lada plus the fused negative (lada phim, lada um). tang lada (only if) states the same condition positively.

items.target: tang lada ___ / katba dang ___
items.gloss: provided that ___ / as long as (time) ___

example.target: Phi lah ban shong hangne tang lada phi ïarap ha ïing.
example.gloss: You can stay here as long as you help in the house.

items.note: tang lada is the condition reading; katba dang (while still) is the time reading. Don't translate 'as long as' with kat, which is only for size.

items.target: lehse ___ / ba lehse ___
items.gloss: in case ___ (perhaps ___)

example.target: Shim ka syrbaïn, lehse kan slap.
example.gloss: Take the umbrella, in case it rains.

items.note: Khasi has no 'in case' conjunction: the precaution is stated, then lehse (perhaps) plus the risk. ba lehse ties the two more tightly in writing.

items.target: uei uei ruh / kaei kaei ruh / shano shano ruh / lano lano ruh
items.gloss: whoever / whatever / wherever / whenever

example.target: Kaei kaei ruh ba phi ong, ngan sngap. Shano shano ruh ba phi leit, ngan leit lem.
example.gloss: Whatever you say, I'll listen. Wherever you go, I'll go along.

items.note: Doubling the question word plus ruh (also) gives the -ever series; ba links it to the clause. uei is 'which (m.)', kaei 'which (f.)', mano mano ruh 'whoever'.

items.target: ym tang ___, hynrei ___ ruh
items.gloss: not only ___, but ___ also

example.target: Ym tang ka slap, hynrei ka lyer ruh ka khlaiñ.
example.gloss: Not only did it rain, but the wind was also strong.

items.note: ym tang (not only) fronts the first item, hynrei plus ruh gives the second. Word order stays flat; the stress lands on ruh.

items.target: wat la ___ ruh, ___
items.gloss: even if ___, ___

example.target: Wat la ka slap ruh, ngin leit.
example.gloss: Even if it rains, we'll go.

items.note: The same wat la as although; ruh after the clause tips it from 'although' (fact) to 'even if' (possibility). Future yn follows in the main clause.

items.target: ka + abstract noun (ka jingieid, ka jingsuk); ki + noun for generic plurals
items.gloss: abstract and generic nouns keep their marker

example.target: Ka jingieid ka long ka jingkhlaiñ. Ki ksew ki ieid ïa ki briew.
example.gloss: Love is strength. Dogs love people.

items.note: Every abstract noun carries ka (or u) even where English has no article: ka jingsuk (peace), ka bor (power). Generic statements use ki: ki khun ki lehkai.

items.target: man ka/u ___ (each, every) / baroh (all) / baroh ar (both) / kawei na ki ar (either) / ym kawei ruh (neither)
items.gloss: each, every, both, all, either, neither

example.target: Man ka sngi nga leit; baroh ki khun ki la wan; baroh ar ki bha; ym kawei ruh kam bha.
example.gloss: Every day I go; all the children came; both are good; neither is good.

items.note: man precedes the marked noun (man u briew, each person); baroh follows or precedes freely. Neither is a negative plus ym kawei ruh (not even one).

items.target: shim ka jingpyrkhat (make a decision), ai ka jingmut (give an opinion), leh ka kam (do the job), pdiang ka jingtrei (take up work), kylli ka jingkylli (ask a question), ïoh ka jingjop (win), ai hukum (give an order), bam kwai (chew betel)
items.gloss: verb-noun pairs to learn as units

example.target: Ngi hap ban shim ka jingpyrkhat mynta ka sngi; u bah u la ai hukum.
example.gloss: We have to make a decision today; the boss gave the order.

items.note: Khasi 'makes' decisions with shim (take) and 'does' work with leh or trei; the light verb is not predictable from English, so learn the pair.

items.target: verb + particle: leit noh (go away), wan biang (come back), mih noh (get out), sah shuh (stay on), dep noh (be over), bam dep (eat up)
items.gloss: particle verbs with noh, biang, shuh, dep

example.target: U la leit noh, hynrei un wan biang lashai. Ka jingbam ka la dep noh.
example.gloss: He has gone away, but he'll come back tomorrow. The food is finished.

items.note: noh (away, off), biang (again, back), shuh (any more, on), dep (finished) follow the verb and change its sense. They stay after the object: bam ïa ka ja dep.

items.target: ka jingshisha (truth), ka daw (reason, cause), ka jingpyrkhat (thought), ka jingmut (opinion), ka jingtip (knowledge), ka jingbha (good, benefit), ka jingsniew (harm, evil), ka jinglaitluid (freedom), ka jingkylla (change), ka jingmyntoi (benefit, profit), ka jingjop (success, victory), ka jingïadei (relation), ka jingsngewthuh (understanding), ka bor (power), ka hok (right, justice), ka jingmynjur (agreement)
items.gloss: Abstract nouns and argument vocabulary
items.note: jing- turns almost any verb or adjective into a noun, and the result is nearly always ka. Argue with ka daw (reason) and u nuksa (example), never with 'point'.

items.target: ka kam (work), ka jingdie-thied (trade), ka kompani (company), ka jingmyntoi (profit), ka jingduh (loss), ka pisa (money), ka spah (wealth), u/ka trai (owner), u/ka nongtrei (employee), ka rukom (method), ka jingïakren (negotiation), ka jingmynjur (agreement), ka kontrak (contract), ka jingsan (growth), ka jingphah (delivery), ka por kut (deadline)
items.gloss: Work, business, negotiation
items.note: die is sell and thied is buy, so ka jingdie-thied is trade. Negotiation is ïakren (talk together); the agreement is ka jingmynjur.

items.target: ka sorkar (government), ka ri (country), ka hima (state, kingdom), ka jaitbynriew (community, people), ki paidbah (the public), ka khubor (news), ka kot khubor (newspaper), ka aiñ (law), u/ka nongïalam (leader), u syiem (chief, king), ka jingsuk (peace), ka jingïarap (help), ka polis (police), ka jingtei (development), ka jingïaid (progress), ka dorbar (council)
items.gloss: Politics, society, news
items.note: ka dorbar shnong is the village council and u syiem the traditional chief; Khasi politics is talked about with these words as much as with sorkar.

items.target: ka sains (science), ka jingtip (knowledge), ka jingpyrshang (experiment), ka jingshem (finding), ka mashin (machine), ka bor (energy, power), ka um (water), ka lyer (air), ka ding (fire, electricity), ka jingshai (light), ka jingkhih (motion), ka jingkylla (change), ka mariang (nature), ka pyrthei (earth), ka komputer (computer), ka dawai (medicine)
items.gloss: Science and technology
items.note: Technical terms are English loans dropped into Khasi grammar with a ka marker: ka sains, ka mashin. Native words cover the elements: um, lyer, ding, khyndew.

items.target: ka jingrwai (song), rwai (sing), ka jingshad (dance), shad (dance), ka kot (book), u/ka nongthoh (writer), ka dur (picture), ka phlim (film), ka jingïalang (festival, gathering), ka Shad Nongkrem (Nongkrem dance), ka riti (custom), ka phawar (Khasi couplet chant), ka ktien (language), ka jingthoh (writing), ka museum (museum), ka jingiathuhkhana (story)
items.gloss: Arts, culture, books, film
items.note: Shad Suk Mynsiem and Shad Nongkrem are the two great dances; phawar are improvised couplets chanted at them. Ka jingiathuhkhana is a story told aloud.

items.target: Sohra (standard, written); Shillong urban (English mixing); Bhoi, War, Maram, Lyngngam dialects; Pnar (Jaintia) as a sister language
items.gloss: Sohra Khasi is the school and Bible standard and what this file teaches. Shillong speech is the same grammar with heavy English mixing and quicker particle fusion. Bhoi, War and Maram villages have different vowels and some different words; War in particular can be hard even for Shillong speakers. Pnar from Jowai is a separate but related language: greetings overlap, grammar words differ.

items.target: final particles hi, noh, te, pat, shuh carry attitude; a flat Bha shibun is sarcastic; a drawn-out hooid is doubt
items.gloss: Attitude lives in the little final words: hi (really, indeed), noh (just, resignedly), te (so then), pat (again, but), shuh (any more). Bha shibun said flat and low is sarcastic; said with a high rise it is delight. A long, falling hooid means 'yes ... I suppose'; a quick hooid hooid is enthusiastic agreement.

items.target: Lah ban ong ba ___ / Don kiba ong ba ___
items.gloss: It can be said that ___ / There are those who say that ___

example.target: Lah ban ong ba ka jingtrei na ïing ka pynduh ïa ka jingïadei ha ophis.
example.gloss: It could be argued that working from home weakens office relationships.

items.note: lah ban ong with no subject is the impersonal 'one can say'. don kiba ong ba (there are those who say) attributes the view to others.

items.target: Shisha hi, ___ / Nga mynjur ba ___
items.gloss: Admittedly, ___ / I grant that ___

example.target: Shisha hi, ka dor ka jrong; hynrei ka jingbam ka bha tam ha Shillong.
example.gloss: Admittedly, the price is high; but the food is the best in Shillong.

items.note: shisha hi (true indeed) fronts the concession and expects a hynrei. Said alone with a fall it is a plain 'that's true'.

items.target: Wat la kumta, ___ / Hynrei pat, ___
items.gloss: Even so, ___ / But then again, ___

example.target: Wat la kumta, ngam pyrkhat ba ngin lah ban leh kane u snem.
example.gloss: That said, I don't think we can do this this year.

items.note: wat la kumta (even though it is so) pivots after a concession; hynrei pat (but again) is the lighter spoken pivot.

items.target: Ha ka lyngkot, ___ / Ban pynkut, ___
items.gloss: In short, ___ / To finish, ___

example.target: Ha ka lyngkot, ka jingpyrkhat ka bha, hynrei ka pisa kam biang.
example.gloss: In short, the idea is good, but the money isn't enough.

items.note: lyngkot is short; ha ka lyngkot fronts the summary. ban pynkut (to close) signals the last point in a speech.

items.target: Nga mynjur ïa kata, hynrei ___ / Nga sngewthuh ïa kata, hynrei ___
items.gloss: I accept that, but ___ / I understand that, but ___

example.target: Nga mynjur ïa kata, hynrei ka por kam biang.
example.gloss: I take your point, but the time isn't enough.

items.note: mynjur ïa kata (agree to that) is stronger than sngewthuh ïa kata (understand that). Both need hynrei to complete the move.

items.target: Phim sngewsih lada nga ___? / Ka long bha lada phi lah ban ___
items.gloss: Would you mind if I ___? / It would be good if you could ___

example.target: Phim sngewsih lada nga pynkhang ïa ka window?
example.gloss: Would you mind if I close the window?

items.note: sngewsih (feel bad) in the fused negative future with lada is the Khasi 'mind if'. The answer Em, wat sngewsih (no, don't feel bad) means 'go ahead'.

items.target: Nga pyrkhat lada phi lah ban ___ / Lada lah, sngewbha ___
items.gloss: I wonder whether you could ___ / If possible, please ___

example.target: Nga pyrkhat lada phi lah ban phah ïa ka kot haduh lashai.
example.gloss: I wonder if you could send the document by tomorrow.

items.note: pyrkhat lada (think whether) softens a request in writing; lada lah (if possible) does it in speech. Both keep the request in phi form.

items.target: Haba peit ïa baroh ar liang, ___ / Ha kaba kut, ___
items.gloss: Looking at both sides, ___ / In the end, ___

example.target: Haba peit ïa baroh ar liang, nga mynjur ban khang ïa ki kali na ka nongbah.
example.gloss: On balance, I agree with banning cars from the city centre.

items.note: peit ïa baroh ar liang (look at both sides) is the balanced verdict opener; ha kaba kut (at the end) is the plainer 'in the end'.

items.target: Kat ba ___, ___ / Ha kawei ka bynta ___ / Ym ha baroh ki kam, hynrei ___
items.gloss: To the extent that ___, ___ / In one part ___ / Not in all cases, but ___

example.target: Kat ba ka kam ka long kaba kordinari, ka AI ka lah ban leh; hynrei ym ha baroh ki kam.
example.gloss: Insofar as the work is ordinary, AI can do it; but not in all cases.

items.note: Uses G-INSOFAR, D-ARGUABLE, G-NEVERTHELESS. kat ba (as far as) fences the claim; ym ha baroh (not in all) is the qualification.

items.target: formal: Nga pan ïa phi ban ___ / neutral: Phi lah ban ___? / casual: Me ___ noh
items.gloss: formal: I request you to ___ / neutral: Can you ___? / casual: just ___

example.target: Nga pan ïa phi ban ap. / Phi lah ban ap khyndiat? / Me ap noh!
example.gloss: I request that you wait. / Can you wait a bit? / Just wait!

items.note: Uses T-REGISTER, D-COULD, T-IMPERATIVE. Register moves along phi versus me/pha, pan (request) versus bare imperative, and the particle noh for casual ease.

items.target: Bha shibun! (flat) / Ban ong jem, ___ / Kumta noh ka ___
items.gloss: Very good! (flat, ironic) / To put it gently, ___ / So much for the ___

example.target: Ka bas ka la lait ar kynta. Bha shibun! Kumta noh ka jingleit jong ngi.
example.gloss: The bus was two hours late. Wonderful! So much for our trip.

items.note: Uses D-SO-MUCH-FOR, C-PUT-IT-MILDLY, D-LITTLE-DID. Irony is mostly tone: praise words said flat and low. Khasi humour prefers understatement to sarcasm.

items.target: To ngi sdang / Lada phi ai lad, ___ / To ngi leit shaphrang / To ngi pynkut hangne
items.gloss: Let's begin / If you allow, ___ / Let's move on / Let's close here

example.target: Lada phi ai lad, Bah, ngin sa wan biang sha kata. To ngi leit shaphrang.
example.gloss: If I may, Bah, we'll come back to that. Let's move on.

items.note: Uses C-IF-I-MAY, C-MOVE-ON, G-GIVEN-THAT. Chairing runs on to ngi (let's) imperatives and lada phi ai lad to interrupt an elder politely.

items.target: Da ka jingburom, ___ / Nga la pyrkhat ba ___ / Lehse ka kham bha lada ___
items.gloss: With respect, ___ / I had thought that ___ / Perhaps it would be better if ___

example.target: Da ka jingburom, Bah, nga la pyrkhat ba ngin sdang na ka dor shwa.
example.gloss: With respect, Bah, I had thought we would start from the price first.

items.note: Uses C-WITH-RESPECT, D-WOULD-HAVE-THOUGHT, G-ALBEIT. Criticism to seniors goes through jingburom (respect), la pyrkhat (past thought) and lehse (perhaps).

items.target: Nga pan shisha ba phi ___ / tang lada ___ / lada em, ngin ___
items.gloss: I firmly ask that you ___ / provided that ___ / if not, we will ___

example.target: Nga pan shisha ba phi phah ha por; lada em, ngin peit biang ïa ka kontrak.
example.gloss: I insist that you deliver on time; if not, we'll review the contract.

items.note: Uses D-SUBJUNCTIVE, G-PROVIDED, D-HAD-I-KNOWN. Conditions are tang lada (only if); consequences follow lada em (if not) with the future yn.

items.target: Haba peit ïa ki daw, ___ / Ka daw kaba khlaiñ tam ka long ___ / Kumta, ___
items.gloss: Weighing the reasons, ___ / The strongest reason is ___ / Therefore, ___

example.target: Haba peit ïa baroh ki daw, kaba khlaiñ tam ka long ka dor; kumta, ngin shim ka ba ar.
example.gloss: Weighing all the reasons, the strongest is the price; so we'll take the second.

items.note: Uses D-HAVING-DONE, G-HENCE, C-ALL-THINGS. Evaluation names ki daw (reasons), ranks with khlaiñ tam (strongest), and concludes with kumta.

items.target: nga la pyrkhat ba ___ / nga la ngeit ba ___
items.gloss: I had thought that ___ / I had believed that ___

example.target: Nga la pyrkhat ba ngin sdang na ka jingpeit jong ki nongthied.
example.gloss: I would have thought we'd start from the customers' view.

items.note: Past la on pyrkhat is the hedge: 'I had thought (so I am surprised)'. Khasi has no 'would have thought'; the past tense plus a soft tone does the work.

items.target: lah ban ong ba ___ / don ka daw ban ___
items.gloss: it can be said that ___ / there is reason to ___

example.target: Lah ban ong ba ka AI kan pynkylla ïa ka kam, hynrei ym baroh.
example.gloss: It's arguable that AI will change the job, but not entirely.

items.note: Impersonal lah ban ong (one can say) hedges the claim; don ka daw ban (there is a reason to) makes the case for an action.

items.target: kham bha nga ___ noh / ka lah shisha ban ___
items.gloss: I might as well just ___ / it may well ___

example.target: Kham bha nga leit noh mynta, ka bas ka lait. Ka lah shisha ban slap janmiet.
example.gloss: I might as well go now, the bus is late. It may well rain this evening.

items.note: kham bha (better) plus noh (just, resignedly) gives 'might as well'. lah shisha ban (can truly) is 'may well'. Neither needs a special verb form.

items.target: ka ong ba ka la ___ / ka ïthuh kumba ka la ___
items.gloss: she says that she has ___ / she looks as if she has ___

example.target: Ka ong ba ka la dep ïa ka kam, hynrei ka ïthuh kumba ka la sdang tang mynta.
example.gloss: She claims to have finished the work, but she seems only to have started now.

items.note: There is no perfect infinitive: 'claims to have' is ong ba (say that) plus la. 'Seems to have' is ïthuh kumba (look as if) plus la.

items.target: nga pyrkhat shisha ba ___ / nga la pyrshang hi ___
items.gloss: I really do think that ___ / I did indeed try ___

example.target: Nga pyrkhat shisha ba ka jingpyrkhat ka bha; nga la pyrshang hi ban ïathuh ïa u.
example.gloss: I do think the idea is good; I did try to tell him.

items.note: Emphasis is an adverb (shisha, truly) or the particle hi (indeed) after the verb, plus stress. There is no 'do'-support to reach for.

items.target: lada nga la tip, ___ / lada phi donkam, ___
items.gloss: if I had known, ___ / should you need, ___

example.target: Lada nga la tip ba ka por kut ka la kylla, ngan la ïathuh ïa ki.
example.gloss: Had I known the deadline had moved, I would have told them.

items.note: Khasi has no inverted conditional; every condition, formal or casual, begins with lada. Formality comes from vocabulary (donkam, pan) not from word order.

items.target: nga pan shisha ba u dei ban ___ / ka donkam shisha ba ka dei ban ___
items.gloss: I firmly ask that he ___ / it is truly necessary that she ___

example.target: Nga pan shisha ba phi dei ban phah ïa ki mar ha por.
example.gloss: I insist that you deliver the goods on time.

items.note: No subjunctive exists: a demand is pan (request) plus shisha (firmly) and a ba clause carrying dei ban (must). ka donkam ba (it is needed that) is the impersonal version.

items.target: nga la thmu ban ___ / nga la dei ban ___
items.gloss: I had planned to ___ / I was to ___

example.target: Nga la thmu ban leit sha Sohra mynhynnin, hynrei ka bas kam shym la mih.
example.gloss: I was going to go to Sohra yesterday, but the bus didn't leave.

items.note: la thmu ban (had planned to) is the future-in-the-past; la dei ban (was supposed to) stresses the arrangement. Both imply it did not happen.

items.target: ynda la ___ dep, nga ___ / hadien ba nga la ___, nga ___
items.gloss: after having ___, I ___ / after I had ___, I ___

example.target: Ynda la dep ïa ka kam, nga la tip ba ki jingdonkam ki la kylla.
example.gloss: Having finished the project, I learned that the requirements had changed.

items.note: There is no participle: the clause is ynda la (once ... had) plus dep, with the subject often left out when it is the same as in the main clause.

items.target: ngam shym la tip ba ___ / ym tang ba ym ___, hynrei ___
items.gloss: I did not know at all that ___ / far from being ___, ___

example.target: Ngam shym la tip ba ki la kylla ïa ka jingdonkam shwa shi taiew.
example.gloss: Little did I know that they had changed the requirement a week before.

items.note: 'Little did I know' is a plain past negative with shym, stressed on tip. 'Far from being X' becomes ym tang ba ym X (not only not X) plus hynrei.

items.target: kumta noh ka ___ / wat pyrkhat shuh ïa ___
items.gloss: so much for the ___ / forget about the ___

example.target: Kumta noh ka jingleit jong ngi sha Sohra. Wat pyrkhat shuh ïa kata.
example.gloss: So much for our trip to Sohra. Never mind that.

items.note: kumta noh (like that, then) with a falling tone dismisses a hope. wat ... shuh (don't ... any more) is 'never mind'.

items.target: tang ynda nga la ___, ___ / nga dang shu ___, ___
items.gloss: no sooner had I ___ than ___ / I had just ___ when ___

example.target: Tang ynda nga la dep ïa ka kam, u bah u la phah ïa ka jingdonkam kaba thymmai.
example.gloss: No sooner had I finished the work than the boss sent the new requirement.

items.note: tang ynda (only once) plus la, then the main event with la. dang shu (still just) plus the verb is the 'had barely' variant. Nothing inverts.

items.target: phi / me, pha; pan ïa phi ban ___ / ___ noh; sngewbha / To ___
items.gloss: formal versus informal versions of the same turn

example.target: Formal: Nga pan ïa phi ban ap. Neutral: Phi lah ban ap? Casual: Ap noh, Bah!
example.gloss: Formal: I request you to wait. Neutral: Can you wait? Casual: Just wait, mate!

items.note: Register is carried by pronoun choice (phi versus me/pha), by pan and sngewbha, and by the particles To (soft) and noh (casual). The verb never changes.

items.target: ba ___ la ___ (that ___ has ___) / ban la ___ (rare, written)
items.gloss: perfect infinitive: a ba clause with la

example.target: Ka ong ba ka la dep ïa ka kam. U ïthuh kumba u la thiah.
example.gloss: She claims to have finished the work. He seems to have slept.

items.note: English 'to have done' becomes a finite clause with la after ba or kumba. ban la is possible in writing but sounds stiff; avoid it in speech.

items.target: no inversion: fronted phrase + normal clause (Ym shym ... / Tang ynda ...)
items.gloss: inversion after negative adverbials does not exist

example.target: Ym shym la don ka por, ngam shym la kren bad u.
example.gloss: Never was there time, so I did not speak with him.

items.note: Fronting a negative phrase for emphasis is fine, but the clause after it keeps subject-verb order. Emphasis is by fronting and stress, not by inversion.

items.target: not applicable: ba + dei ban ___ / lada + bare verb / To + verb
items.gloss: no subjunctive; obligation and wish use dei ban, lada, To

example.target: Ka donkam ba ki dei ban wan. To long ka jingsuk!
example.gloss: It is necessary that they come. May there be peace!

items.note: Where English keeps a subjunctive (that he be, if I were, long live), Khasi uses dei ban inside a ba clause, lada plus the bare verb, or the To wish-imperative.

items.target: la thmu ban ___ / la dei ban ___ / reported: ba ___ yn ___ (unchanged)
items.gloss: future in the past: had planned to, was supposed to; yn stays in reports

example.target: U la ong ba un wan, hynrei u la dei ban leit sha ophis.
example.gloss: He said he would come, but he was supposed to go to the office.

items.note: In reports the future yn stays as it was said (un wan, he would come). For a plan that did not happen use la thmu ban or la dei ban.

items.target: Wat la kumta ruh, ___ / Kumta ruh, ___
items.gloss: Even so, ___ / Nonetheless, ___

example.target: Ka dor ka jrong; wat la kumta ruh, ngin thied.
example.gloss: The price is high; nevertheless, we'll buy.

items.note: wat la kumta (even though it is so) plus ruh is the strongest concession link. Kumta ruh alone is the short form; hynrei is the everyday one.

items.target: wat la ___ / la ___ ruh
items.gloss: albeit ___ / even though ___

example.target: Ka jingpyrkhat ka bha, wat la ka thymmai eh.
example.gloss: The idea is good, albeit rather too new.

items.note: Khasi has one concessive, wat la, for although, even if and albeit. After a noun phrase it takes an adjective directly: wat la thymmai eh.

items.target: kat ba ___ / haduh ba ___
items.gloss: as far as ___ / to the extent that ___

example.target: Kat ba nga tip, ka kam ka dang ïaid; kat ba ki lah, ki la ïarap.
example.gloss: As far as I know, the work is still going; to the extent they could, they helped.

items.note: kat ba (as much as) fences a claim; kat ba nga tip (as far as I know) is the daily hedge. haduh ba (up to where) is the written variant.

items.target: haba peit ba ___ / namar ba ___
items.gloss: seeing that ___ / given that ___

example.target: Haba peit ba ka por kam biang, to ngi shim tang ki kam kiba kongsan.
example.gloss: Given that time is short, let's take only the important items.

items.note: haba peit ba (when one sees that) presents a known fact as the reason; namar ba is the plain because. Both leave word order untouched.

items.target: wat la ___ ruh, ___ / khlem peit ïa ___
items.gloss: notwithstanding ___ / regardless of ___

example.target: Khlem peit ïa ka dor, ngin thied kane ka ïing.
example.gloss: Regardless of the price, we'll buy this house.

items.note: khlem peit ïa (without looking at) is 'regardless of' before a noun; wat la ... ruh handles a whole clause. No single formal preposition exists.

items.target: kumta, ___ / namarkata, ___ / da kata, ___
items.gloss: hence, ___ / for that reason, ___ / thereby, ___

example.target: Ka bas ka la lait; kumta, ngi la sah ha ïing.
example.gloss: The bus was late; hence, we stayed at home.

items.note: kumta (thus) is the neutral result link, namarkata (because of that) the formal one, da kata (by that) is 'thereby'. All sit sentence-initially.

items.target: khnang ba ym ___ / ba ym ___
items.gloss: so that not ___ / lest ___

example.target: Ïaid suki, khnang ba phim hap.
example.gloss: Walk slowly, lest you fall.

items.note: There is no 'lest': purpose khnang ba plus the fused negative (phim, um, kam). For fear that is namar ba sheptieng ba (because of fear that).

items.target: tang lada ___ / ha ka jingkhat ba ___
items.gloss: only if ___ / on the condition that ___

example.target: Ngin sah bad kane ka kompani tang lada ki phah ha por.
example.gloss: We'll stay with this company provided that they deliver on time.

items.note: tang lada (only if) is the everyday 'provided that'. ha ka jingkhat ba (on the condition that) is contract language; jingkhat is a condition or rule.

items.target: jing- + verb (ka jingpyrkhat, ka jingtrei, ka jingtip) / nong- + verb (agent) / ka daw ba ___ (the fact that)
items.gloss: nominalisation with jing- and nong-

example.target: Ka jingshim jingpyrkhat jong ki ka la wan lait; ka daw ba ki la ap ka pynsniew ïa ka kam.
example.gloss: Their decision came late; the fact that they waited harmed the work.

items.note: jing- makes the action noun, nong- the doer (nongtrei, worker), and both keep ka or u. 'The fact that' is ka daw ba, literally 'the reason that'.

items.target: noun + kaba/uba + adjective chain; jong for stacked possessors; no pre-modification
items.gloss: formal noun phrases build to the right

example.target: Ka jingpyrkhat kaba thymmai bad kaba khlaiñ jong ka sorkar ka hima Meghalaya.
example.gloss: The new and strong policy of the Meghalaya state government.

items.note: Khasi cannot stack adjectives before a noun: every modifier follows with kaba/uba, and possessors chain with jong. Long noun phrases read left to right.

items.target: nga ruh (so do I) / ngam ruh (neither do I) / nga kyrmen ba em (I hope not) / hooid, nga ruh
items.gloss: ellipsis and substitution with ruh

example.target: Nga ieid ïa ka jadoh. — Nga ruh. Ngam ieid ïa ka tungrymbai. — Ngam ruh.
example.gloss: I like jadoh. — So do I. I don't like tungrymbai. — Neither do I.

items.note: Pronoun plus ruh replaces the whole verb phrase, with the fused negative when needed (ngam ruh). 'I hope so' is nga kyrmen kumta, 'I hope not' nga kyrmen ba em.

items.target: object or adverb first, then the normal clause; ïa ___ stays on a fronted object
items.gloss: fronting for emphasis

example.target: Ïa ka jadoh nga ieid, ïa ka tungrymbai em. Mynhynnin hi u la wan.
example.gloss: Jadoh I like, tungrymbai not. It was only yesterday that he came.

items.note: Anything can move to the front for contrast, keeping its ïa or ha; the rest stays in place. hi after the fronted word adds 'precisely'.

items.target: bam kwai ha dwar U Blei (chew betel at God's door: to die), tip briew tip Blei (know man, know God: the moral code), kamai ïa ka hok (earn righteousness), ka ïing ka sem (house and home), ki khun ki ksiew (children and grandchildren), ka ri ka shnong (land and village), ka ktien ka thylliej (word and tongue), ka mynsiem ka rngiew (spirit and aura), ka jingsuk ka jingsain (peace and comfort), ka bor ka jingkhlaiñ (power and strength), ka jingim ka jingïap (life and death), ka kti ka kjat (hands and feet: labour)
items.gloss: Idioms and fixed metaphors in daily use
items.note: Khasi idiom loves paired nouns (ka ïing ka sem) that say one idea twice; use them whole. tip briew tip Blei and kamai ïa ka hok are the two maxims everyone knows.

(come) / To wan, sngewbha (do come), u briew (man) / u rangbah (gentleman, elder), ka kynthei (woman) / ka kmie (mother, respectful), pisa (cash) / spah (wealth), bam (eat) / bam ja (take a meal), ïing (house) / ïing sem (home)
items.gloss: Register pairs: casual and formal words for the same thing
items.note: Formality in Khasi is mostly address (phi, Bah, Kong, Mei) and particles (To, sngewbha) rather than a separate vocabulary; the pairs above are the exceptions.

items.target: pynjot (destroy), pynkhreh (prepare, repair), pynbeit (correct), pyniaid (operate, run), pynshai (clarify), pyllait (release), pdiang (receive), pynkhlaiñ (strengthen), ïarap (help), kyrpad (plead, pray), kynmaw (remember), klet (forget), pyrshang (attempt), pynkylla (transform), pynkut (conclude), batai (explain)
items.gloss: Low-frequency precise words
items.note: The causative prefix pyn- turns intransitives into precise transitives: beit (straight) gives pynbeit (correct); shai (bright) gives pynshai (clarify). Learn the root and the pyn- form together.

items.target: rkhie (laugh), pynrkhie (make laugh), ka jingrkhie (laughter, joke), lehkai (play, joke), kren lehkai (speak in jest), shu ong (just saying), shisha ne lehkai? (serious or joking?), ka phawar (witty couplet), sngewrem (embarrassed), ka jingsngewkmen (fun), kren jem (speak gently, understate), bha shibun (wonderful, ironic when flat)
items.gloss: Humour, irony, understatement
items.note: Khasi teasing is lehkai; ask shisha ne lehkai? when unsure. Phawar couplets at dances are the traditional home of wit, and the ironic tone is flat, not exaggerated.

items.target: ka jingwad (research), ka jingpyrshang (experiment), ka jingshem (finding), ka jingthoh (paper, writing), ka jingpyni (presentation), batai (explain), ka jingbatai (explanation), ka daw (reason), u nuksa (example), ka jingmut (meaning), ka jingpynshai (clarification), ka kot (document), ka rukom (method), ka jingtip (knowledge), ka jingsngewthuh (understanding), ka jingpynkut (conclusion)
items.gloss: Academic and professional discourse
items.note: Academic Khasi builds nouns with jing- from plain verbs (wad, search; pyni, show; batai, explain). English terms are borrowed freely alongside them.

items.target: contrast by fronting plus stress; hi and pat after the stressed word; lengthening the stressed vowel
items.gloss: Khasi marks contrast by moving the contrasted phrase to the front and lengthening its stressed final syllable, often with hi (precisely) or pat (on the other hand) right after it: Ïa ka JADOH hi nga ieid. Pitch does less work than in English; word order and the particles do more. A quiet, low delivery signals seriousness, not boredom.

items.target: flat, low, slightly slow delivery of praise words; a stretched hooid; noh with a fall
items.gloss: Irony is a flat, low, unhurried Bha shibun or Bha hi where enthusiasm would rise. A stretched hoo-oid with a fall means 'sure it is'. noh on a fall (kumta noh) is resignation. Listen for praise vocabulary delivered without the rise, and for laughter that follows it.

items.target: Wat la kumta, ___ / La kumta ruh, ___
items.gloss: Be that as it may, ___ / Even so, ___

example.target: Wat la kumta, ngi hap ban shim ka jingpyrkhat mynta ka sngi.
example.gloss: Be that as it may, we have to decide today.

items.note: wat la kumta (even though it is so) is the formal pivot back to the main line; la kumta ruh is the same with the concessive la ... ruh frame.

items.target: Ban ong jem, ___ / Ban kren suki, ___
items.gloss: To say it gently, ___ / To speak softly, ___

example.target: Ban ong jem, ka jingphah ka la lait khyndiat.
example.gloss: To put it mildly, the delivery was a little late.

items.note: jem is soft or gentle; ban ong jem fronts an understatement, and khyndiat (a little) inside the clause carries the irony.

items.target: Da ka jingburom, ___ / Map ïa nga, Bah, hynrei ___
items.gloss: With respect, ___ / Forgive me, Bah, but ___

example.target: Da ka jingburom, Bah, ngam pyrkhat ba kane ka rukom kan trei.
example.gloss: With respect, Bah, I don't think this method will work.

items.note: burom is honour; da ka jingburom (with respect) is followed by the senior's title (Bah, Kong) and then the disagreement in phi form.

items.target: To ngi leit shaphrang / Ngin sa wan biang sha kata
items.gloss: Let's move forward / We'll come back to that later

example.target: Khublei, Kong. Ngin sa wan biang sha kata; to ngi leit shaphrang sha ka kam ba ar.
example.gloss: Thanks, Kong. We'll come back to that; let's move on to the second item.

items.note: shaphrang is forward; to ngi leit shaphrang is the chair's move-on. sa wan biang (come back later) parks a point without rejecting it.

items.target: Lada phi ai lad, ___ / Map, lada nga lah ban ong, ___
items.gloss: If you allow, ___ / Excuse me, if I may say, ___

example.target: Lada phi ai lad, Bah, nga kwah ban wan biang sha ka agenda.
example.gloss: If I may, Bah, I'd like to return to the agenda.

items.note: ai lad (give way) is 'allow'; lada phi ai lad is the polite interruption, especially to elders, and is followed by the title.

items.target: Pynbeit ïa nga lada nga bakla, hynrei ___
items.gloss: Correct me if I'm wrong, but ___

example.target: Pynbeit ïa nga lada nga bakla, hynrei ka por kut ka la long ka sngi Friday, ne em?
example.gloss: Correct me if I'm wrong, but the deadline was Friday, wasn't it?

items.note: pynbeit (make straight) is correct; bakla is 'wrong, mistaken'. The tag ne em at the end keeps it a question rather than a challenge.

items.target: Haba pyrkhat ïa baroh, ___ / Ha kaba kut, ___
items.gloss: Considering everything, ___ / In the end, ___

example.target: Haba pyrkhat ïa baroh, kane ka long ka jingpyrkhat kaba bha tam.
example.gloss: All things considered, this is the best option.

items.note: pyrkhat ïa baroh (think over everything) is the weighing phrase; bha tam (best) is the usual verdict adjective.

items.target: Lada ka lah ban ïarap, ___ / Tang ka jingmut jong nga, hynrei ___
items.gloss: If it can help, ___ / This is only my opinion, but ___

example.target: Lada ka lah ban ïarap, nga la ju leh kane ka kam shwa.
example.gloss: For what it's worth, I have done this job before.

items.note: There is no idiom: Khasi says what the offer is worth (if it can help) or disclaims it (only my opinion). Both front the hedge before the point.

scenarios.alt: Ha kawei ka bynta ka dei; hynrei ym ha baroh ki kam. Ka Khasi ka don khyndiat eh ka data, kumta u briew u dang donkam.
scenarios.tip: kat ba fences the claim; the counter after it needs wat la kumta ruh rather than a bare hynrei to sound weighed.

model.target: Nga pan shisha ba phi dei ban phah ha por. Ngin sah bad phi tang lada kane kam jia biang; lada phi la lait shuh, ngin peit biang ïa ka kontrak.
model.gloss: I insist that you deliver on time. We'll stay with you provided this doesn't happen again; should you be late again, we'll review the contract.

breakdown.text: Nga pan shisha ba phi dei ban
breakdown.label: D-SUBJUNCTIVE · pan shisha ba + dei ban

breakdown.text: ngin peit biang ïa ka kontrak.
breakdown.label: slot: consequence · fut

scenarios.alt: Ka donkam shisha ba ki mar ki dei ban poi ha por. Ha ka jingkhat ba kane kam jia shuh, ngin sah; lada em, ngin khang ïa ka kontrak.
scenarios.tip: There is no subjunctive: the demand is pan shisha plus a ba clause with dei ban, and every condition, however formal, starts with lada.

model.target: Ynda la dep ïa ka kam, nga la ïathuh ïa u bah. Tang ynda nga la ong, u la ïathuh ba ki jingdonkam ki la kylla. Kumta, nga hap ban sdang biang.
model.gloss: Having finished the work, I told the boss. No sooner had I spoken than he told me the requirements had changed. Hence, I have to start again.

scenarios.alt: Hadien ba nga la pynkut ïa ka kam, nga la tip ba ki la kylla ïa ka jingdonkam shwa shi taiew; namarkata baroh ka kam ka la long khlem kam.
scenarios.tip: Khasi has no participle or inversion: ynda la ... dep and tang ynda ... la carry both, with subject-verb order untouched.
